function: Learned digital precoding for a massive-MIMO LEO satellite downlink, maximizing energy efficiency: end-to-end GNN and GNN-based deep unfolding of Dinkelbach-WMMSE (pp. 1, 3).
system: LEO satellite with 8x8 UPA (64 antennas, fully digital) serving K=10 single-antenna users, downlink, 2 GHz carrier, 20 MHz bandwidth; no RIS (pp. 3, 11).
method: Edge-update GNN (MLPs) trained end-to-end; deep-unfolded Dinkelbach-WMMSE with GNN Taylor-expansion matrix inverse; unsupervised, loss = negative EE, Adam, lr 0.01 (pp. 5-6, 10-11).
data_channel: Own simulated LEO channel from the model of [38] (Doppler, delay, array response, statistical CSI), MATLAB-generated; 10,000 training and 1,000 test channel matrices (pp. 3-4, 11).
test_conditions: Defaults 8x8 UPA, K=10, 10,000 training and 1,000 test channels; Fig. 12 trained at Nt=64, zero-shot K=8-24; antenna and CSI-error sweeps (pp. 11-13).
baselines: Non-learned: WMMSE, RZF, MMSE (instantaneous CSI). Learned: linear deep unfolding of WMMSE following [40]; end-to-end GNN is the authors' own variant (pp. 11-13).
metrics: Energy efficiency (Mbits/Joule) versus power budget, antennas, users and CSI error; EE histogram; execution time versus users and antennas (pp. 11-13).
complexity: Order of complexity and FLOP count (pp. 6, 10-11), claiming O(K Nt^2) instead of O(K Nt^3) for inversion; measured execution time on an i7-13700 CPU (pp. 11-12).
q1_support: p. 3: "the frequency response of the complex baseband channel at frequency f can be expressed as [38]". Custom LEO channel (Eqs. 1-3, pp. 3-4); Table I (p. 11) lists no 3GPP, QuaDRiGa or measured data, and QuaDRiGa [43] is cited only for equal path angles (p. 4).
q2_support: p. 12: "deployment across varying user scales". The same sentence says the networks were trained at Nt = 64 and deployed zero-shot; Fig. 12 (p. 13) varies K from 8 to 24 users while Table I (p. 11) lists K = 10.
q3_support: p. 11: "we incorporated regularized zero forcing (RZF) and minimum mean square error (MMSE) methodologies employing instantaneous CSI". Fig. 11 (p. 12) compares EE of WMMSE, RZF, MMSE (non-learned) with linear deep unfolding of WMMSE after [40] (learned, earlier work).
q4_support: p. 11: "The total FLOP count for the GNN amounts to" a sum over layers, followed by the order of complexity of the deep unfolding algorithm; execution times are measured in Figs. 8-9 (pp. 11-12).
q5_support: p. 11: "scipy.io.loadmat to convert MATLAB-generated .mat files into tensors". The data are the authors' own simulated channels (10,000 train, 1,000 test); no code or data link and no public dataset is mentioned.
notes: Area 6 rather than 3: the learned precoder controls beams and power of a LEO satellite downlink for energy efficiency, and 6 precedes 3 in the specificity order; the 8x8 satellite array means the single-antenna check does not apply. The linear deep unfolding baseline follows [40]; the end-to-end GNN is a variant of the proposed method and is not counted for q3. The reviewer should confirm that linear deep unfolding counts as an earlier learned method and not as an ablation of the proposed GNN unfolding. q2 rests on one sentence (p. 12); Fig. 11 (antenna counts) does not say whether the model was retrained. The PDF is the arXiv v1 preprint (6 May 2025) and does not print the DOI.
